chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad and Ahmad, the sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from al-Fadl ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from one of them, who said:

Regarding a man who has a pregnant wife and wishes to divorce her, he said: 'If he intends the divorce explicitly, he divorces her in the presence of witnesses. If it occurs to him on that day or afterwards that he wishes to exercise the right of return (raj'a), let him return and consummate (the marriage). Then if it occurs to him that he wishes to divorce again, he divorces her. Then if it occurs to him that he wishes to return, he returns as he returned first. Then if it occurs to him that he wishes to divorce again, she becomes the one who is not permissible to him [for a simple return] until she marries another husband.' This is when, upon returning, he intends consummation and retention, and he consummates.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on divorcing a pregnant wife and the conditions for her remarriage to the same husband?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanics of *Talaq al-Raj'i* (revocable divorce) for a pregnant wife, stressing that the husband's intent must be explicit and witnessed to ensure validity. It details the cycle of revocation and finalization, culminating in the *Talaq al-Mu'abbad* (irrevocable divorce) which triggers the *Ghar'* condition, requiring the wife to marry another man before she can return to her first husband.
